title: Can lift variations/accessories affect your form on the main lifts?
summary: NH discusses whether variations and accessories can change technique on the main lifts. Many variations (deficit deadlifts, pause squats, pause bench, front squats) help form, but some (stiff-leg deadlifts, good mornings, box squats) can reinforce bad patterns, especially if they fully replace the main lift. Keep training the main lift and pick variations that target your individual weak points.

claims.claim: Variations of the main lifts can change your form on them, for better or worse.
Deficit deadlifts help lifters who lack leg drive learn to push with the legs and hip hinge properly.

Lifters like him who already have strong leg drive and use a lot of quads in the deadlift do not need deficit pulls; it only reinforces an already strong habit. They need more hip-hinge work or simply more deadlifts.
Snatch-grip deadlifts also use more quads, but he keeps them because they develop his upper back so well that the trade-off is worth it.
Stiff-leg deadlifts can become a bad habit carried into the conventional deadlift; many people already pull what is effectively a stiff-leg deadlift (too little knee flexion, bar too far forward).

Regardless of leverages and proportions, pulling a deadlift with your torso parallel to the floor is never proper form; you need a neutral back and some torso angle before you pull (Olympic lifting setups differ).
Light paused squats help correct shooting the hips back out of the hole and knee valgus, because knee angle is easier to control with lower weight.
Paused bench is one of the best variations for improving bench press form.
Front squats are mostly beneficial for the back squat: they force you upright, create core rigidity, teach leg drive and keep the thoracic spine from rounding.
If you replace back squats entirely with good mornings, your back squat will degrade into a 'good morning squat' because your body adopts the pattern.
The fix is to do both: replace one squat session with good mornings. Good mornings help many people's squat, including his, adding strength and allowing more volume.
Box squat cycles do not fix back-squat form: most people sit back too far, rock on the box and good-morning the weight up, getting stronger at using the box rather than better at squatting.
Advising box squats to lifters with too much thoracic rounding in the back squat is a mistake.
It is tempting to focus on variations that suit your strengths because being strong is fun, but you should train your weak points; his are the top portion of the deadlift, not the floor.
Whether powerlifter or bodybuilder, you must focus on your weak points to bring them up.
As long as you keep working on the main lift itself and do not expect a variation to cure it, form deterioration will never become unfixable.

exercises.name: Deficit deadlift
exercises.why: teaches leg drive and hip hinge to those lacking it; unnecessary for quad-dominant pullers

exercises.name: Snatch-grip deadlift
exercises.why: great upper back development despite more quad involvement

exercises.name: Stiff-leg deadlift
exercises.why: can bleed into conventional deadlift form as a bad habit

exercises.name: Conventional deadlift
cues: neutral back, torso not parallel to floor

exercises.name: Paused squat
cues: keep hips from shooting back out of the hole
exercises.why: corrects hip shoot and knee valgus

exercises.name: Paused bench press
exercises.why: one of the best variations for bench form

exercises.name: Front squat
exercises.why: teaches leg drive and upright posture for back squat

exercises.name: Good morning
exercises.why: helps squat strength and volume, but should not fully replace back squats

exercises.name: Box squat
exercises.why: criticised: people rock and good-morning off the box, doesn't fix form
